text:
maria: ran a short nsys trace on the batcher+kvcache hotpath. timeline looks like: large H2D memcpy bursts on stream 1, then kernels on stream 2, with ~10-40ms CPU gaps between kernel launch and actual work. attaching png and the nsys snapshot link.

anil: can you paste the nsys command you ran? curious about flags + timeline so we can check stream ids.

maria: sure — command:```bash
nsys profile --trace=cuda,cudnn,osrt --sample=none -o /tmp/trace 
  --capture-range=duration:0.0:5.0 
  --output=true ./run_reproducer --batch-size=8 --seq-len=512
```
I also recorded NVTX around prefetch + handoff. trace: https://internal-traces/1943214567/overview (png: https://img.internal/1943214567.png)

jess: quick glance: those memcpys on stream 1 look like they're being forced onto the default stream (so they serialize). can you check if allocator / prefetch path is using stream 0 or an explicit stream? :eyes:

maria: good call. i grep'ed the prefetch path — found a refactor where we pass stream=nullptr into the pinned-copy helper, and the helper calls cudaMemcpyAsync(..., 0). oops. that would put them on the legacy default stream and block other streams on the device depending on stream semantics.

anil: that also explains the CPU gaps: we launch kernel on worker thread -> push NVTX -> but the copy on default stream forces a synchronization point on the device before the kernel can proceed, so the CPU thread yields for a bit waiting on queue space. see this snippet from the timeline: kernel_enqueue at t=1.452s, kernel start at t=1.495s, memcpy (default stream) occupying 1.460-1.488s — overlap looks like cuda stream semantics causing serialization.

maria: repro: changed helper to accept cudaStream_t and pass batcher stream. quick local run shows memcpy now on stream 3, kernel on stream 2, visible overlap and kernel starts earlier. latency down ~12% on that trace.

jess: nice. two followups: 1) we should audit other callsites of that helper (likely in prefetcher + eviction path), 2) add an assert in debug build forcing non-zero stream when called from async contexts.

perf-bot: automated note: created perf ticket PERF-1298 with trace link and attached screenshot.

anil: also annotate the trace with stream-level counters — run with:```bash
nsys profile --trace=cuda,osrt --sample=none --export=nvtx --output=trace_streams ./run_reproducer
```
then open in nsight and enable "CUDA API" table to see which API enqueued the copy.

maria: will push the helper fix + audit PR today and run a set of nsys traces across multi-batch sizes. will post before/after traces in thread. thanks for the quick eyes. :thumbsup:

jess: if it lands, let's also add a small perf regression test to CI that runs a short nvprof/nsys check and fails if default-stream copies are introduced on the hotpath. preventing regressions saved us here.

maria: agreed — adding test to eng-runtime/ci/perf-smoke.

anil: great, mark resolved here for the trace. reopen if you see similar patterns in other traces.

maria: closing loop — fix merged in PR #4321, perf traces show overlap restored and CPU gaps reduced.
